title: Rays Overcome Brewers in 12th, 2‑Run Rally Secures Game 5 Spot in World Series (4‑3)
body:
The Tampa Bay Rays escaped elimination in Game 4 of the World Series, rallying in the bottom of the 12th inning to beat the Milwaukee Brewers 4‑3 and force a decisive Game 5. After a tense, scoreless extra‑innings stretch, Jonny DeLuca’s single and a clutch pinch‑hitter strike from Ben Williamson sent the winning run home, capping a dramatic comeback that snapped Milwaukee’s chance to clinch its first championship.

Milwaukee entered the final frame with a three‑run lead and just three outs away from a historic title. Junior Camerino’s grounder to third base opened the bottom of the 12th, but the Brewers’ defense could not contain the Rays’ surge. After a leadoff walk, the Rays loaded the bases with a single and a sacrifice bunt, setting the stage for the decisive at‑bat. DeLuca’s pinch‑hit single drove in the go‑ahead run, and Williamson’s subsequent single brought home the winning run, sending the stadium into a frenzy and leaving Brewers fans stunned.

The victory was a testament to Tampa Bay’s resilience and depth. Starting pitcher Nathan Eovaldi, who had been solid through seven innings, surrendered three runs in the eighth, prompting manager Kevin Cash to turn to a bullpen that had been shaky all series. Yet the relievers held firm long enough for the offense to mount its comeback. The decisive home run in the ninth, delivered by rookie Cooper Pratt, had already given the Rays a 3‑2 edge before the Brewers tied it in the tenth, illustrating the back‑and‑forth nature of the series.

For Milwaukee, the loss is a painful reminder of how quickly momentum can shift in baseball’s ultimate stage. The Brewers’ offense, which had been potent throughout the series, was stymied by Tampa Bay’s strategic pitching changes and defensive positioning. Manager Craig Counsell’s decision to keep junior reliever Junior Camerino on the mound for the 12th inning—a move that initially seemed to secure the win—backfired when the grounder turned into a pivotal moment. The Brewers will need to regroup quickly, focusing on tightening their bullpen execution and sharpening situational hitting as they head into Game 5.

The series now stands at a 2‑2 tie, with both clubs possessing a mix of veteran poise and youthful firepower. Tampa Bay’s ability to manufacture runs in high‑leverage situations underscores the value of depth in its roster, while Milwaukee’s reliance on timely hits highlights the thin line between triumph and defeat. Analysts point to the Rays’ aggressive baserunning and willingness to use pinch‑hit specialists as a strategic edge, whereas the Brewers must address their late‑inning defensive lapses if they hope to capitalize on their offensive strengths.

Looking ahead, Game 5 will likely be a turning point. Tampa Bay will aim to sustain the confidence gained from their extra‑inning heroics, while Milwaukee will seek redemption by reasserting the dominance they displayed early in the series. The next contest promises to be a showcase of pitching duels, clutch hitting, and managerial chess moves, with the World Series trophy hanging in the balance. Both teams now know that every decision, from the bullpen mound to the pinch‑hitter’s bat, can tip the scales in this tightly contested championship.
